text:
anna-support: heads up — customer ACME reported a sharp p99 regression on /v1/generate starting ~09:20 UTC. baseline ~700ms -> now ~3.2s. they sent a small-payload workload (short prompts).

ops-bot: incident created #INC-2026-145, alerting on p95/p99 for route=acme-prod.

sam-sre: thanks. can you paste their traffic shape and example request? any deploys around 09:00-09:30?

anna-support: traffic shape: lots of tiny prompts (<=16 tokens). 80% single-turn short prompts. no deploys flagged by deploy-bot between 08:45-09:30. sample request: 
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer xxxxx' -d '{"model":"rwd-13b","prompt":"Summarize my note","max_tokens":32}'
```

maria-ml: short prompts + continuous batching == classic hold-window tail. what's our current route config for batching (batch_size vs max_wait_ms vs grace_window)?

jordan-platform: pulling route config now. route(acme-prod): continuous.batcher.enabled=true, batch_size_target=16, batch_size_max=64, max_wait_ms=60, grace_window_ms=120, prefetch_kv=true.

lee-eng: ping — seeing a big increase in fraction of batches with size=1. p50 batch_size=1, p90=3. tiny prompts are dominating and the hold timeout is keeping requests waiting for coalesce -> when a large request finally arrives it blows out p99.

sam-sre: do we have queueing metrics? show me per-instance p99 and batch wait time distribution.

jordan-platform: past 30m metrics: mean batch_wait_ms increased from ~8ms to ~74ms, p95 batch_wait_ms ~310ms, queuing counts spike on nodes serving acme-prod. per-instance p99 latency correlated with batch_wait_ms peaks.

anna-support: customer reported spike right after they turned on a small-feature flag that increases parallel API clients. could be microburst. they can throttle but want quick mitigation from our side.

maria-ml: probable root cause: microburst of tiny requests + aggressive grace_window + prefetch interplay. prefetch can increase scheduling jitter because it primes KV cache and nudges model hot paths—when combined with long max_wait_ms we get larger variance.

lee-eng: quick repro steps I used locally: spin up continous-batcher sim with 90% single-token requests at 400rps for 2m. observe p99 jump when a 12-token request arrives that forces kernel switch. repro script: 
```
# python-ish pseudocode
for i in range(0,400):
  send_request(prompt='hi', max_tokens=8)
  sleep(0.0025)
# after 60s send occasional 12-token request to trigger longer exec path
```

sam-sre: ok real quick mitigation options: 1) reduce max_wait_ms for route to 12ms (aggressively favor lower latency, costs up), 2) lower grace_window_ms to 20ms, 3) route-level policy to bypass continuous batching for tiny payloads (disable for prompts < 24 tokens), 4) fallback to small-model variant for bursts.

jordan-platform: we can hotpatch route config. command: `redwoodctl routes update acme-prod --set continuous.batcher.max_wait_ms=12 --set continuous.batcher.grace_window_ms=20` and can target 10% canary then 100% in 5m.

anna-support: customer prefers quick p99 fix. they approved temporary latency-priority change.

lee-eng: I'll apply 10% canary to isolate regressions. monitoring: track p50/p95/p99 and token-cost delta.

ops-bot: deploy started for route acme-prod canary=10% by lee-eng (change id: cfg-8812).

sam-sre: after canary, if p99 drops to ~900ms we roll to 100%. if not, rollback and try disabling prefetch_kv.

(10m later)

lee-eng: canary: p99 dropped from 3.2s -> 1.05s, p95 back to ~420ms, cost per request +8%. no errors. scaling looks stable.

anna-support: relayed to customer, they're seeing improvement in their end-to-end traces as well. :relieved:

maria-ml: follow-up: need a long-term fix — options: adaptive hold-window based on payload size, or per-tenant batching policy that disables coalescing for tiny prompts and instead uses immediate dispatch. also consider automatic model-path switching to keep kernel consistency for mixed request sizes.

sam-sre: file a tech-debt ticket to add route-level policy `batch_policy: size_aware` and probe adaptive max_wait heuristics. record repro script + metrics.

jordan-platform: created ticket PLAT-3498 with logs, repro script, and config diff. tagging: @maria-ml @lee-eng @sam-sre.

ops-bot: incident #INC-2026-145 resolved (mitigated) — follow-up required for permanent fix.

lee-eng: remaining action items: 1) implement size-aware batching experiment, 2) add metric alert for batch_size_skew, 3) document quick mitigation steps in runbook. I'll draft runbook PR after lunch. :coffee:

anna-support: thanks all. customer confirmed p99 back to acceptable range. closing escalation on our side after runbook PR.
